claims.text: Headline: Lebanon gets ten days of peace (Israel-Lebanon ten-day ceasefire)
claims.note: Bloomberg video: Trump says Israel and Lebanon agreed to a 10-day ceasefire; also PBS/AP https://www.pbs.org/newshour/world/israel-and-lebanon-reach-10-day-ceasefire-agreement-trump-says. 'Peace' is figurative; it is a truce.

claims.text: Headline: Myanmar cuts Aung San Suu Kyi's sentence in half
claims.note: SCMP: 27-year term cut by 4.5 years (one-sixth), not by half. The body's own figure contradicts the headline.

claims.text: Subheadline: dictatorships offer mercy and democracies broker truces, someone is preparing for worse things
claims.note: Rhetorical speculation, no source.

claims.text: Ben Roberts-Smith granted bail in Australia while facing war crimes charges over Afghanistan
claims.note: AP wire (on ABC News site): granted bail 17 April 2026 on five counts of war crime murder over killings of Afghans in 2009 and 2012.

claims.text: Roberts-Smith was once Australia's most decorated living veteran / former SAS soldier
claims.note: AP calls him Australia's most decorated veteran; former SAS soldier per Reuters copy at thestar.com.my.

claims.text: Prosecution case built around 'a culture of impunity that ran from Kabul to Canberra'
claims.note: Editorial characterisation, not in the reports. Removed.

claims.text: Myanmar junta cut Suu Kyi's sentence by four and a half years in a 'broad-ranging amnesty deal', according to SCMP
claims.note: SCMP headline: cuts prison term by 4 1/2 years in broad-ranging amnesty deal; amnesty also freed former president Win Myint (4,335 prisoners).

claims.text: The junta's mercy suggests they need money from the international community
claims.note: Speculation, no source.

claims.text: Israel and Lebanon agreed to a ten-day ceasefire according to Bloomberg
claims.note: Bloomberg video, 17 April 2026.

claims.text: Middle East Eye reports Israel carrying out 'massive' demolitions in south Lebanon despite the truce
claims.note: Libnanews item crediting Middle East Eye: 'Israel carries out massive demolition in south Lebanon despite ceasefire' (Khiam). MEE original live-blog URL not located; CNN satellite review also found demolitions continued after 16 April.

claims.text: Macron warns the ceasefire is 'already undermined'
claims.note: Macron's actual words on X: concern that it 'may already be undermined by the continuation of military operations' (Naharnet/AFP https://cdn.naharnet.com/stories/en/319597-macron-says-lebanon-israel-ceasefire-may-already-be-undermined). Quote corrected to 'may already be undermined'.

claims.text: Tens of thousands are returning to southern Lebanon
claims.note: MEE: thousands return to south Lebanon after ceasefire, defying Israeli warnings; other reports (Anadolu) say tens of thousands. Copy uses 'thousands'.

claims.text: Asian markets fell on the fragile nature of Middle East peace, per CNBC
claims.note: Fall confirmed by AP (on KSAT). CNBC article not found after two searches; attribution changed to AP.

claims.text: CNBC as source of the Asian markets report
claims.note: Could not locate the CNBC piece; reattributed to AP.

claims.text: Conflict & Security sentiment 54/100; global sentiment 61/100
claims.note: internal feed metric, not reportable

claims.text: Bitcoin sentiment 70/100, market signal 50
claims.note: internal feed metric, not reportable

claims.text: Crypto ignores everything except Federal Reserve policy and Elon Musk tweets
claims.note: Unsourced generalisation. Removed.

claims.text: Vietnamese airlines agreed to lease up to 10 C909 jets from Chinese manufacturers
claims.note: SCMP: one Vietnamese airline (Vietjet) to lease up to 10 C909 jets. Lessor is SPDB Financial Leasing, not the manufacturer (https://centreforaviation.com/news/vietjet-air-signs-lease-agreement-for-10-comac-c909-aircraft-1355673). Copy corrected to singular airline, Chinese-made jets.

claims.text: Beijing's campaign to break the Boeing and Airbus duopoly
claims.note: Editorial framing, not sourced. Removed.

claims.text: Hong Kong flagged oil tankers are testing US blockades in the Strait of Hormuz
claims.note: SCMP: one Hong Kong-flagged tanker (AVA 6) passed through the strait in a test of the US blockade. Copy uses singular.

claims.text: DW News coverage of Trump taking credit for Pope Leo's election
claims.note: playlist/video pick, not news. DW item not found; Trump did post that 'if I wasn't in the White House, Leo wouldn't be in the Vatican' (Daily Beast). Dropped.

claims.text: Pope Leo is a pontiff who doesn't exist
claims.note: Pope Leo XIV was elected in May 2025. The edition's claim of an editorial error is false.

edits.headline: Israel and Lebanon agree to ten-day ceasefire
edits.subheadline: President Trump said Israel and Lebanon had agreed to a ten-day ceasefire, Bloomberg reported.
editorialBody: Israel and Lebanon agreed to a ten-day ceasefire, President Trump said, according to Bloomberg. Thousands of displaced people returned to south Lebanon after the truce took effect, Middle East Eye reported.

Israel carried out large-scale demolitions in south Lebanon despite the ceasefire, according to Middle East Eye. French President Emmanuel Macron said he supported the ceasefire but was concerned it "may already be undermined" by continuing military operations, Naharnet reported.
Myanmar cut Aung San Suu Kyi's prison term by four and a half years in a broad amnesty that also freed former president Win Myint, the South China Morning Post reported.
In Australia, former SAS soldier Ben Roberts-Smith was granted bail on five charges of war crime murder over killings in Afghanistan, the Associated Press reported.
Asian stocks and oil prices fell on 17 April, the Associated Press reported.

Vietjet agreed to lease up to 10 Chinese-made C909 jets, the South China Morning Post reported. A Hong Kong-flagged oil tanker passed through the Strait of Hormuz in a test of the US blockade, the SCMP reported.
